raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County, so I will keep doing what fits my land, water, and labor best: a winter wheat and summer maize rotation. That is the most steady choice for me. Our area is on the North China Plain, and this double-cropping system is familiar, practical, and easier for me to manage with my experience. I will not spread my land across many crops, because that makes field work, fertilizer use, irrigation, and pest control harder to manage. I would rather keep a simple plan with crops I know well and with yields I can count on.

For winter wheat, I will use improved seed because it is more reliable than old seed I save myself, but still familiar to grow. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage after the summer maize harvest, apply base fertilizer, sow in autumn, irrigate a few key times, and control weeds and diseases when needed. After the wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize on the same land. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because maize hybrids usually give better yield and stronger performance. I will use less tillage before maize if time is short after wheat harvest, keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate mainly at important growth stages if water is available, and spray only when pest pressure is real. This way, I keep costs under control and aim for stable grain output over the whole year.
